output_list.reason: The mintToken function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The initial supply is set in the constructor, minted to the owner, and can be minted to any target address by the owner, without overflow checks. This can lead to unexpected minted token distribution.

The transfer function has a wrong logic in _transfer function: assert(balanceOf[_from] + balanceOf[_to] == previousBalances);. The assert function will always be true due to integer overflow, allowing the owner to set the balanceOf[_from] to a negative value, and the balanceOf[_to] to a very large value.

The burnFrom function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The _value is not checked to be greater than the allowance[_from][msg.sender], allowing a contract with very high allowance to set the balance of the caller to a negative value.
The setPrices function has a typo in it, it should be 'setPrices' but it is 'setPri ces'. This can make the function uncallable, and it is a common vulnerability in token smart contracts.
